title.narrative: Youth for Sustainable Tourism and Conservation around World Heritage Sites in Tanzania.

description.narrative:
“Youth for Sustainable Tourism and Conservation around World Heritage Sites in Tanzania” aims at strengthening the engagement of young people in the promotion of sustainable tourism and conservation around World Heritage Sites in Tanzania. The engagement responds to the growing need to involve communities, particularly youth, in heritage conservation and sustainable development processes while supporting national priorities in tourism, culture, community participation, and youth empowerment.
Tanzania is home to seven World Heritage Sites of outstanding universal value, including natural and cultural heritage sites that contribute significantly to national identity, biodiversity conservation, tourism development, and local livelihoods. However, many communities living around these sites, especially young people, continue to face limited opportunities to actively participate in heritage-related decision-making, sustainable tourism activities, and awareness programmes. At the same time, increasing pressures related to environmental degradation, limited awareness on conservation, and socio-economic challenges continue to affect the sustainability of heritage sites and the communities surrounding them.
The engagement will build on and scale up previous UNESCO-supported activities that have demonstrated the important role of youth and communities in heritage conservation and sustainable development. It draws on lessons learned from the project implemented at the Kilimanjaro National Park World Heritage Site, which supported the establishment of Youth Conservation Ambassadors and strengthened youth engagement in conservation awareness, climate action, and community outreach. The engagement will also build synergies with the UNESCO–TUI Care Foundation partnership for sustainable tourism in Zanzibar, particularly the activities being implemented in and around the Stone Town of Zanzibar World Heritage Site. Through activities such as Youth Heritage Ambassadors and the “Sounds and Stories of Stone Town” programme, young people are being engaged in storytelling, cultural promotion, creative entrepreneurship, and heritage-based tourism development. By leveraging the experiences, networks, and good practices emerging from these activities, the engagement will further strengthen the capacity of youth to become champions of sustainable tourism, conservation, and community participation around World Heritage Sites in Tanzania, while promoting inclusive opportunities for local communities to benefit from responsible tourism development.
The engagement seeks to strengthen awareness and participation of youth in sustainable tourism and conservation through capacity-building activities, dialogue platforms, storytelling approaches, and community engagement initiatives. Participants will be introduced to key concepts related to World Heritage, sustainable tourism, conservation, community participation, and responsible heritage promotion.
The activities will further support youth-led awareness engagements aimed at promoting responsible tourism practices and conservation awareness within local communities. The engagement contributes to the implementation of the UNESCO World Heritage Convention by promoting awareness, community participation, and sustainable approaches to conservation and tourism development around World Heritage Sites. It also supports national priorities related to tourism promotion, youth empowerment, and the sustainable management of cultural and natural heritage resources.
